title: Inject metadata when creating a filesystem symlink for a non-symlink artifact.

timeline.body:
A ctx.actions.symlink whose output is a declare_file or declare_directory
(as opposed to a declare_symlink) has "copy" semantics, i.e., the output
artifact is indistinguishable from the referent except for its name; the
symlink is just a filesystem-level optimization to avoid an actual copy,
and is transparently resolved when collecting the action output metadata.

When the symlink points to an artifact that was built remotely and without the
bytes, we currently must download it before executing the symlink action, so
that the output metadata can be constructed from the local filesystem. This
change short-circuits the filesystem traversal by injecting output metadata,
which is identical to the input plus a pointer to the original path. This is
used by the prefetcher to avoid downloading the same files multiple times when
they're symlinked more than once.

(An alternative would have been to teach all of the RemoteActionFileSystem
methods to resolve symlinks by patching together the local and remote metadata,
but that would have resulted in an awful lot of complexity.)

Fixes #15678.

reply.body: Oops, it was a leftover from a previous refactor. Removed.

timeline.body: What about output that is symlink? I know we are going to handle it differently, but should we throw an error here?

reply.body:
If the output is a symlink, then we should create the symlink and not inject any metadata. Skyframe will later call `readSymbolicLink` and not attempt to resolve it.

Unfortunately, unresolved symlinks don't currently work together with remote execution because of other issues, so I can't add an integration test for it (I did add a unit test to verify that `createSymbolicLink` and `readSymbolicLink` round-trip when the output is of type symlink).
That makes sense. Do we allow actions to access undeclared output (i.e. create undeclared symlink in this case)?

Yes, undeclared symlinks are created via `ctx.actions.symlink(output = declare_symlink(...))` which works today. They can also be consumed as inputs to other actions.

I suspect we should also inject the metadata for undeclared symlinks into Skyframe (`UnresolvedSymlinkArtifactValue` seems to have been introduced for that exact purpose, but is mysteriously unused in the codebase). However, I don't want to expand the scope of this PR to include it, so for now I'm still creating an actual symlink in the local filesystem.

Sorry for didn't make it clear, but my question was about **undeclared** output not **unresolved** symlink. To be more specific, do we want to move line `super.createSymbolicLink()` inside the check `if (output != null)` and instead throw an error there to prevent actions create **undeclared** outputs?

timeline.body:
Potentially, we could download the same files twice. e.g. symlink `a` points to file `b`, but the metadata are same from the perspective of skyframe.

When staging inputs for actions that requires `a`, we download `a` and create files instead of symlinks on the local file system. Then we do the same thing for actions that requires `b`. It is getting worse if the target is directory. This is another reason why we currently creating a dangling symlink for the internal equivalent.

reply.body: Per offline discussion, I've added a `stagingExecPath` field to `RemoteFileArtifactValue`, which is used by the input prefetcher to avoid downloading the same file more than once. This is a bit of a hack, but the alternatives all seem excessively complex to me.

Let me write down what we have discussed just now:
- For file, the `stagingExecPath` is used to store the path of final target file. We might want to rename it to a better name to reflect the fact that this remote metadata is actually a symlink to another remote metadata. Alternative way is to create a subclass of `RemoteFileArtifactValue`. I'm fine with either way.
- For tree, we don't want to store `stagingExecPath` in remote metadata for every `TreeFileArtifact`. We can store it in an extra field of `TreeArtifactValue` or in a subclass.
- We resolve symlink chains to the last target when injecting the metadata in the `createSymbolicLink`. So when we staging the symlink in the prefetcher, we know the `execPath` of final target (This is what you are doing now, just write it down for clarification).
- For symlinks whose targets are on the local file system (i.e. remote metadata for the target is `null`), we don't inject metadata but just create symlinks on the local files system.
- We need to update the serialization/deserialization code for remote metadata in https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/actions/cache/CompactPersistentActionCache.java.
- We are interested in the test case: `sym` points to a `dir/file` (by `declare_file`) inside a `dir` (by `declare_dir`)
  - are we able to deduplicate the downloads of `dir/file`?

I might miss some other points but you get the idea.

PTAL. Some points of note:

- Naming: I've settled on `symlinkTargetExecPath` instead of `stagingExecPath`. I think that's as explicit as it gets :)
- Skyframe values: I've added a `symlinkTargetExecPath` field to the existing `TreeArtifactValue` (whose size remains at 40 bytes due to padding) and introduced a new`SymlinkToRemoteFileArtifactValue` subclass (to avoid increasing the size of `RemoteFileArtifactValue`). Following a suggestion by Alex, the metadata for tree artifacts is retrieved via `TreeArtifactValue#getMetadata`, which avoids adding a `MetadataProvider#getTreeArtifactValue` method.
- Nested artifacts: I've added tests for them in `BuildWithoutTheBytesIntegrationTest`, but as we discussed, the prefetcher currently isn't able to deduplicate the downloads (and the downloads might even collide). Since this is a preexisting issue and nested artifacts are relatively rare, I'd prefer to fix it outside of this PR. It has been filed as #16333.

timeline.body: Do we have the case where the tree is not entirely remote? If so, how do we handle that?

reply.body: No, I don't believe this could ever occur, since two actions cannot produce the same tree artifact. So I think `!isEntirelyRemote` effectively means "is entirely local".

reply.body: Introduced a separate `SymlinkToRemoteFileArtifact` subclass to avoid increasing the size. For `TreeArtifactValue`, we got lucky and the new field fits within the preexisting padding, so no subclass is required.

timeline.body: Consider using [createWritableDirectory](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/d44d4ea960fdc7260977e69b530e053baebf7fb8/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/vfs/Path.java#L436-L448) to get it all done in 1 call.
As we talked offline, you may be better off returning a FileMetadataValue from `getMetadata` which includes that so you can just request that using `metadataProvider.getMetadata(treeArtifact)`.

reply.body: Thanks, this made everything so much simpler!

+  @Test
+  public void symlinkToSourceFile() throws Exception {
+    addRemoteModeOptions();
+    addOutputModeOptions();
+
+    write(
+        "a/defs.bzl",
+        "def _impl(ctx):",
+        "  if ctx.attr.chain_length < 1:",
+        "    fail('chain_length must be > 0')",
+        "",
+        "  file = ctx.file.target",
+        "",
+        "  for i in range(ctx.attr.chain_length):",
+        "    sym = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.label.name + '.sym' + str(i))",
+        "    ctx.actions.symlink(output = sym, target_file = file)",
+        "    file = sym",
+        "",
+        "  out = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.label.name + '.out')",
+        "  ctx.actions.run_shell(",
+        "    inputs = [sym],",
+        "    outputs = [out],",
+        "    command = '[[ hello == $(cat $1) ]] && touch $2',",
+        "    arguments = [sym.path, out.path],",
+        "    execution_requirements = {'no-remote': ''} if ctx.attr.local else {},",
+        "  )",
+        "",
+        "  return DefaultInfo(files = depset([out]))",
+        "",
+        "my_rule = rule(",
+        "  implementation = _impl,",
+        "  attrs = {",
+        "    'target': attr.label(allow_single_file = True),",
+        "    'chain_length': attr.int(),",
+        "    'local': attr.bool(),",
+        "  },",
+        ")");
+
+    write(
+        "a/BUILD",
+        "load(':defs.bzl', 'my_rule')",
+        "",
+        "my_rule(name = 'one_local', target = 'src.txt', local = True, chain_length = 1)",

+    write("a/src.txt", "hello");

+  }
